title: Descent of the full tensor bifunctor shift structure and normalized fixed comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived category $D(R)$ and homotopy localization $Q_h:K(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], which commutes with shifts [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Let $\mathcal P_R\subset K(R)$ be the flat-term K-flat complexes [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex], and assume $\mathcal P_R$ is stable under every integer shift. Use the published total-tensor-derived bifunctor $T$ and its natural representative isomorphisms $c_{P,S}:Q_h\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R S)\cong T(Q_hP,Q_hS)$, resolving localization equivalence and arbitrary-transformation extension property [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Total tensor means [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].
There exist unique natural isomorphisms $t^1_n:T(M[n],N)\cong T(M,N)[n]$ and $t^2_n:T(M,N[n])\cong T(M,N)[n]$ for all integers $n$ and $M,N\in D(R)$, whose restrictions along $Q_h|_{\mathcal P_R}\times Q_h|_{\mathcal P_R}$ are $Q_hs^1_n,Q_hs^2_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], conjugated by $c$ and the canonical shift comparisons of $Q_h$. They satisfy the zero-shift and addition-of-shifts identities. For every pair of integers $a,b$, the two maps $T(M[a],N[b])\to T(M,N)[a+b]$ obtained by extracting shifts in the two orders differ by $(-1)^{ab}$ under the canonical identification of iterated shifts. Thus $t^1,t^2$ give one coherent integer bifunctor shift structure on this specified $T$.
For every derived morphism $f:M\to M'$, the transformation $T(f,-)$ commutes with $t^2_n$; for every derived morphism $g:N\to N'$, $T(-,g)$ commutes with $t^1_n$. These include chain maps between resolving complexes, inverses of their quasi-isomorphisms, and arbitrary words in their localization, independently of the chosen word.
Fix $A\in\mathcal P_R$ and put $H_A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R B)$ and $H^A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_R A)$, assumed to induce functors on $K(R)$ preserving quasi-isomorphisms and equipped with $s^2_n,s^1_n$. Any natural isomorphisms $e_{L,B}:Q_hH_A(B)\cong T(Q_hA,Q_hB)$ and $e_{R,B}:Q_hH^A(B)\cong T(Q_hB,Q_hA)$ whose components on $B\in\mathcal P_R$ are exactly $c_{A,B},c_{B,A}$ commute with the signed shifts for every $B\in K(R)$. Consequently the restrictions of $t^2,t^1$ at $Q_hA$ agree, under these comparisons, with the one-variable shifts descended from $H_A,H^A$. No boundedness is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the existing source-library theorem Functor.commShift₂OfLocalization to the homotopy quotient in both variables, using the published tensorDescentComplexIso. Postcomposition of signed bifunctors with the additive quotient preserves the mixed sign. This equips the published homotopy tensor with its coherent signed integer shifts.

proof.text: The assumed shift stability induces shifts on the full resolving subcategory. Its inclusion commutes with shifts. Restrict the homotopy tensor to this subcategory and postcompose with Qh. The published resolving localization equivalence makes the restricted Qh a localization. Apply Functor.commShift₂OfLocalization again using tensorDescentDerivedIso, obtaining shifts on exactly the specified published derived tensor, with zero, addition, mixed sign and naturality already proved by that general theorem.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS and 06YU; categories.tex Tag 04VK.

proof.text: For either variable, the liftingIsoApp theorem says that each of the two localization comparisons commutes with shifts. Paste these two squares. Naturality of the Qh shift comparison moves the complex-to-homotopy comparison through it. The quotient shift comparison and the full-subcategory inclusion shift comparison are identities on objects; the canonical quotientCompQhIso identifies the remaining comparison with that of Q. This gives exactly tensorResolvingShiftCompatible for tensorDescentPair. For uniqueness choose resolving representatives isomorphic to both arbitrary derived objects, use naturality of both candidate transformations along their product isomorphism, and cancel its invertible image.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS and 06YU; categories.tex Tag 04VK.

proof.text: For a normalized fixed-factor comparison the required shift square on a resolving varying argument is the normalization formula just proved, since its shift is still resolving. For any varying complex B choose a flat-term K-flat resolution f:P to B. Its shift is a quasi-isomorphism. Quasi-isomorphism preservation by the fixed tensor functor makes its localized shifted image invertible. Naturality of the comparison and of both shift comparisons identifies the two sides of the square at B after precomposition with that image with the equal sides at P. Cancel it. Repeat with the tensor order reversed. The resolution theorem states termwise exactness of the categorical tensor-right functor. Use the canonical siteSheafTensorRightIso of [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] and invariance of exactness under natural isomorphism to obtain precisely the IsFlatOnSite predicate in TensorFlatRepresentative.

I read every cited statement: site-derived-tensor-descent (equivalence, c natural on P_R, faithful/unique extension of transformations for any E), total-tensor-integer-shifts (Mathlib leaf; checked against BifunctorShift.lean:95-98 and 199-205, negOnePow(x*y)), homotopy-category-triangulated (CommShift λ), abstract-derived-category, lem-pc-kflat-resolution (= Stacks 06YS, sites-cohomology.tex:3207-3211), and localization-universal-property (1)-(3). I also read Stacks 0FNH (more-algebra.tex:18385-18395): its sign (-1)^{pb} uses the unshifted degree and agrees with the leaf. Steps 1, 2 and 4-8 are correct; I recomputed them myself. The Step 4 summand computation gives (-1)^{bp} versus (-1)^{b(p+a)}, ratio (-1)^{ab}. In Step 6, substituting δ² into α_P cancels to β_P. In Step 7, the resolution r: P→B and v = QH(r[n]) invertible give α_B = β_B by cancellation, with only the varying argument resolved. In Step 8, uniqueness in the universal property identifies t^2(QA,-) with the descended one-variable shift. Edge cases checked: one-point site over a field (Koszul signs), characteristic 2, n=0 and negative shifts, the zero ring, unbounded complexes, and a non-flat B such as Z/2. The parent kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated cites the item's unchanged clauses. No SGA is cited and there is no cycle. I added one sentence: rewrite by naturality of t^i_b along λ_a(P): L(P[a]) → (LP)[a], with P[a] in P_R, to reach δ^i_b(P[a],S). Step 4 relies on the same reduction through its reference to Step 3.
